messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: New unmarked version 1.5.0
parts:
Hi all,

A new version of unmarked (1.5.0) is now on CRAN. It may take some time before packages are available on all platforms.

Changes:

* Added community occupancy model (occuComm); i.e., occupancy model with species-level random effects [1]. See the vignette here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/occuComm.html
* Support for hazard key function in IDS()
* Updates, improvements, standardization for many unmarkedFit methods such as getP, fitted, residuals, ranef, simulate, etc. IMPORTANT: these changes may break old code in some rare cases [2].
* Improved documentation for the functions above
* Bugfixes, including a fix to the goccu() likelihood discussed here: https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked/c/iH6yhkH_tFc


[1] Technically it was already possible to fit this model with the available random effects tools in occu(). The new function makes specifying the inputs and processing the model outputs easier.

[2] I try very hard to not break backwards compatability, but I feel it was necessary in this case. Historically methods for examining fitted models such as fitted(), residuals(), and ranef() have inconsistently handled missing values, particularly cases where all observations for a site were missing. By default, sometimes these sites were dropped and other times they were retained in the output. So if you had 100 sites and one had all missing values, some functions returned output of length 99 and others returned output of length 100. Going forward the output dimensions should always match the inputs - sites with all missing values will never be dropped. As part of these changes, 'na.rm' arguments for these methods will now be ignored. My strong opinion is that handling missing values in the output of these functions should be done by the user, not the package, to minimize the chances of unexpected behavior. Note that this changes nothing about how missing values are handled *when fitting the model* - this still works the same way. These changes apply only to functions liked residuals, ranef, etc. that are used on already fitted models.

Please let me know if you run into any issues with the new version.

Thanks,

Ken

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] New unmarked version 1.5.0
parts:
Rahul,

No, unmarked doesn't currently support the Hines 'tiger on a trail' model. We've talked about supporting this in the past and I'd like to do so eventually. I can't promise any particular timeline for when I'd get to it, though.

Ken

Ken,

Thank and congratulations!  As Marc said, this is a hugely useful bit of software and I'm always grateful for all the support Unmarked and its users get.

Anam,

A good place to start is the vignettes (examples) included in the package.  There are plenty of online resources for how to access R vignettes generally, and working through the ones for the models you might be interested in should help orient you.

-Alex

Rahul

Rahul,

No, unmarked doesn't currently support the Hines 'tiger on a trail' model. We've talked about supporting this in the past and I'd like to do so eventually. I can't promise any particular timeline for when I'd get to it, though.

Ken

On Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 02:26:17PM +0530, Rahul G wrote:
> Dear Ken,
>
> Thank you for the update. I sincerely appreciate your continuous support
> and guidance.

> Apologies if this has already been discussed earlier, but just want to
> understand, if in any possible way the new version of unmarked supports
> models that account for spatial dependence among spatial replicates,
> specifically following the approach of Hines et al. (2010).

> Kind regards,
> Rahul

> > Best regards  ---  Marc
> >
> > ------------------------------
> > *From:* unma...@googlegroups.com <unma...@googlegroups.com> on behalf
> > of Ken Kellner <con...@kenkellner.com>
> > *Sent:* Tuesday, February 11, 2025 00:58

> > *Subject:* [unmarked] New unmarked version 1.5.0
> >
> > Hi all,
> >
> > A new version of unmarked (1.5.0) is now on CRAN. It may take some time
> > before packages are available on all platforms.
> >
> > Changes:
> >
> > * Added community occupancy model (occuComm); i.e., occupancy model with
> > species-level random effects [1]. See the vignette here:
> > https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/occuComm.html
> > * Support for hazard key function in IDS()
> > * Updates, improvements, standardization for many unmarkedFit methods such
> > as getP, fitted, residuals, ranef, simulate, etc. IMPORTANT: these changes
> > may break old code in some rare cases [2].
> > * Improved documentation for the functions above
> > * Bugfixes, including a fix to the goccu() likelihood discussed here:
> > https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked/c/iH6yhkH_tFc
> >
> >
> > [1] Technically it was already possible to fit this model with the
> > available random effects tools in occu(). The new function makes specifying
> > the inputs and processing the model outputs easier.
> >
> > [2] I try very hard to not break backwards compatability, but I feel it
> > was necessary in this case. Historically methods for examining fitted
> > models such as fitted(), residuals(), and ranef() have inconsistently
> > handled missing values, particularly cases where all observations for a
> > site were missing. By default, sometimes these sites were dropped and other
> > times they were retained in the output. So if you had 100 sites and one had
> > all missing values, some functions returned output of length 99 and others
> > returned output of length 100. Going forward the output dimensions should
> > always match the inputs - sites with all missing values will never be
> > dropped. As part of these changes, 'na.rm' arguments for these methods will
> > now be ignored. My strong opinion is that handling missing values in the
> > output of these functions should be done by the user, not the package, to
> > minimize the chances of unexpected behavior. Note that this changes nothing
> > about how missing values are handled *when fitting the model* - this still
> > works the same way. These changes apply only to functions liked residuals,
> > ranef, etc. that are used on already fitted models.
> >
> > Please let me know if you run into any issues with the new version.
> >
> > Thanks,
> >
> > Ken

parts:
Hi Anam, 

There are lots of resources available online for learning RStudio and unmarked itself. I'd recommend the unmarked package website and RSwirl for learning about unmarked and R coding respectively. There are a lot of other resources out there about occupancy modeling as well, it can get very complex very quickly, but for the sake of just learning how to run a model and how to code in R the linked resources can be very helpful. 

Jordan

On Monday, February 10, 2025 at 5:06:10 PM UTC-7 anam.a...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi,
Can anyone help in running simple single species occupancy model using r studio and unmarked ,
I’m very new to this . Need help
Anam 🍀

On Feb 10, 2025, at 17:58, Ken Kellner <con...@kenkellner.com> wrote:

﻿Hi all,


A new version of unmarked (1.5.0) is now on CRAN. It may take some time before packages are available on all platforms.

Changes:

* Added community occupancy model (occuComm); i.e., occupancy model with species-level random effects [1]. See the vignette here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/occuComm.html
* Support for hazard key function in IDS()
* Updates, improvements, standardization for many unmarkedFit methods such as getP, fitted, residuals, ranef, simulate, etc. IMPORTANT: these changes may break old code in some rare cases [2].
* Improved documentation for the functions above
* Bugfixes, including a fix to the goccu() likelihood discussed here: https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked/c/iH6yhkH_tFc


[1] Technically it was already possible to fit this model with the available random effects tools in occu(). The new function makes specifying the inputs and processing the model outputs easier.

[2] I try very hard to not break backwards compatability, but I feel it was necessary in this case. Historically methods for examining fitted models such as fitted(), residuals(), and ranef() have inconsistently handled missing values, particularly cases where all observations for a site were missing. By default, sometimes these sites were dropped and other times they were retained in the output. So if you had 100 sites and one had all missing values, some functions returned output of length 99 and others returned output of length 100. Going forward the output dimensions should always match the inputs - sites with all missing values will never be dropped. As part of these changes, 'na.rm' arguments for these methods will now be ignored. My strong opinion is that handling missing values in the output of these functions should be done by the user, not the package, to minimize the chances of unexpected behavior. Note that this changes nothing about how missing values are handled *when fitting the model* - this still works the same way. These changes apply only to functions liked residuals, ranef, etc. that are used on already fitted models.

Please let me know if you run into any issues with the new version.

Thanks,

Ken
